title: The 10 Best Motorcycle Lifts
subtitle: Scissor jacks, hydraulic lifts, and lift tables for motorcycles and ATVs, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A motorcycle lift gets both wheels off the ground for tire, chain, and suspension work. Amazon sells three kinds: crank scissor jacks around $55 to $70, foot-pedal hydraulic jacks from $125 to $450, and full lift tables near $1,600 that raise the bike to standing height. We ranked 10 on star rating, review volume, and features (hydraulic lift, included tie-downs, casters, and a lift height of 15.5 inches or more).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Goplus Motorcycle Lift, "15000 LBS" Hydraulic ATV Scissor Jack with Footplates, 4.7 to 15 in.
avoid.verdict: It's an ordinary 1,500 lb hydraulic jack sold under a 15,000 lb headline. The VEVOR hydraulic jack has the same lift range and real capacity, costs about $10 less, and has 80 times the reviews.
reasons: The title says 15,000 lb. The spec table and the first bullet both say 1,500 lb. Anyone shopping by the headline number is comparing against a figure that's off by a factor of ten.
Its 4.7 to 15 in. range and 1,500 lb rating match the VEVOR hydraulic jack exactly, so there's nothing it does better for the extra money.
The rear wheels are directional only and the listing names no caster locks, so the jack relies on a hand knob to stay put.

buyers_guide.a: A scissor jack ($55 to $105 here) cranks up with a handle or socket, and it's cheap, light, and reliable. A hydraulic jack ($125 and up) lifts with a foot pedal, usually rolls on casters, and is much faster and easier with a heavy cruiser or bagger. Both get the wheels off the ground; neither puts the bike at standing height.

buyers_guide.q: Will a jack fit under my bike?
buyers_guide.a: Check ground clearance under the frame. Scissor jacks here start at 3.5 to 3.7 in. Most hydraulic jacks need 4.5 to 4.9 in., and the OTC 1545 starts at 3.5 in. Bikes with full lower fairings or exhausts under the frame may need a jack with adapters or a lift table.

buyers_guide.q: How high does it need to go?
buyers_guide.a: To pull a rear wheel you usually need the tire 2 to 4 in. off the ground, which most jacks here manage at 13 to 16 in. If you want to work standing up, you need a lift table like the APlusLift, or the VEVOR 350 lb lift for dirt bikes (up to 36 in.).

Yes. A bike on a center jack can tip sideways when you break loose an axle nut. The VEVOR and VIVOHOME hydraulic jacks and the OTC 1545 include ratchet straps; for the others, run straps from the handlebars to the floor or a wall anchor.
For nearly every motorcycle, yes. Big touring bikes run around 900 lb wet. The 1,500 lb jacks give more margin for heavy baggers and ATVs.
